summary.text: A 50-year-old male kidney transplant recipient with chronic kidney disease, post-transplant diabetes and hypertension, hospitalized in November 2023 for acute kidney injury and mixed transplant rejection treated with rituximab, immunoglobulin and methylprednisolone, presented with malaise, cough and dyspnea that worsened despite outpatient moxifloxacin. Examination showed decreased air entry with Velcro crackles at the left base and laboratory abnormalities including creatinine 5.22 mg/dL.

Chest CT showed multiple pneumonia foci and bilateral pleural effusion, and a sputum panel was positive for Staphylococcus aureus. Bronchoscopic biopsy pathology confirmed Cryptococcus gattii, and blood cultures later confirmed disseminated cryptococcosis. HIV and hepatitis serology were negative, and cranial CT with lumbar puncture showed no evidence of CNS involvement.

He received linezolid, liposomal amphotericin B and fluconazole, with flucytosine and meropenem added, underwent a left lower lobectomy and later a left pneumonectomy for severe left upper lobe bronchial stenosis, and had a neurological decline, intubation, an upper gastrointestinal bleed, atelectasis, and a Trichosporon asahii infection after tracheostomy.

A vegetative state was declared on the 50th hospital day with multiple organ failure; the family signed an advance directive, palliative care was initiated, and the patient died on the 53rd day of hospitalization, 75 days after symptom onset.
